correctness.rationale: The reverse two-step epoch matrix is M^T because individual gradient matrices are symmetric. Independent epoch permutations yield the exact PSD-preserving covariance update T(X)=1/2(MXM^T+M^TXM). Its spectral radius is the positive-cone Perron eigenvalue, so strict contraction on PSD covariances is equivalent to convergence for all deterministic starts. The small-step Lyapunov operator associated with H1+H2>0 is stable, hence the first positive det(I−T)=0 crossing gives the initial stability interval, and a PSD fixed covariance at the boundary certifies nondecay for some rank-one deterministic start. Four fresh independent exact symbolic specializations verify det(I−T)=αβη³(1−x)F1F2/4; the concrete quartic root was counted exactly by Sturm analysis. Finite symbolic specializations corroborate, not replace, the general algebra in the reviewed proof.

final_claim: For two noiseless rank-one quadratic component losses in R² with α,β>0 and nonparallel directions x=<u1,u2>² in (0,1), independently randomizing their order each epoch, the initial interval of epoch-start mean-square convergence is exactly 0<η<η*, where η* is the first positive root of the stated cubic F1 or quartic F2. At the boundary some deterministic initial state does not decay. Example α=2,β=1,x=1/2 gives η*=1.3096734019... exceeding 2/α.
